dossier.purpose: Packaging repo (Dockerfile templates, Bash entrypoints, config templates, Compose samples) that runs Interactive Brokers' IB Gateway, and a desktop-based tws-rdesktop image, unattended in a container. IBC automates the login dialogs, Xvfb provides a virtual display, and socat (or an outbound SSH tunnel) republishes the IB TWS API socket. Images are built per release channel (stable/latest) and published to GHCR and Docker Hub for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The documented way to define and run it is Docker Compose: docker-compose.yml (service ib-gateway) and tws-docker-compose.yml (service tws), started with `docker compose up` (README.md:165-167, 597). Each Compose file defines a single service; supporting services (Jupyter Quant, SSH bastion) are only referenced in the README (README.md:428-441), not defined in the repo.

claims.claim: A docker image to run Interactive Brokers Gateway and TWS without any human interaction on a docker container

Includes IB Gateway (stable or latest), TWS (from 10.26.1h), IBC (simulates user input), Xvfb virtual framebuffer, optional x11vnc, xrdp/xfce for TWS, and socat to relay the API port because IB Gateway restricts connections to the container's 127.0.0.1
Optional remote SSH tunnel (ssh client only, the container does not run sshd) for the IB API and VNC; available from 10.19.2g-stable / 10.25.1o-latest
Supports parallel execution of live and paper trading mode (TRADING_MODE=both)
Secrets support: if a _FILE variable is defined, that file supplies the credential (docker secrets)
aarch64 support (Raspberry Pi, M1/M2/M3) using IBKR's linux-arm installer; `docker compose up` pulls the matching architecture; the TWS arm image 'might have unexpected bugs'
Images ib-gateway and tws-rdesktop in channels latest (10.51.1a) and stable (10.50.1e) with IBC 3.24.2; tags are the channel name, major.minor and the full version
Define services in a docker-compose.yml (or add ib-gateway to an existing one) plus a .env file, then start with `docker compose up`
Sample compose exposes the API and VNC ports only on 127.0.0.1 of the docker host; removing '127.0.0.1:' exposes them to the host network (not recommended)
The IB API is an unencrypted, unauthenticated raw TCP socket; for remote use add TLS or an SSH tunnel; other services on the same docker network can reach it by hostname ib-gateway
The image does not contain or store credentials; they are provided as environment variables at startup and the host must protect them
State: set TWS_SETTINGS_PATH plus a volume to preserve settings across containers; CUSTOM_CONFIG=yes lets you mount your own jts.ini and config.ini
The Dockerfile fetches the IB Gateway installer from this project's GitHub releases, not IB's site, so a specific version can be rebuilt
Custom start-up scripts can run before X (START_SCRIPTS), after X (X_SCRIPTS) and after IBC (IBC_SCRIPTS) from a mounted directory

install.method: Prepare the env file for Compose (Linux; README says to start from .env-dist)
Docker Compose, ib-gateway image (pre-built image from ghcr.io; compose also contains a build section)
Docker Compose, TWS desktop image (same command pulls the arm64 variant on aarch64 hosts)

install.command: docker pull ghcr.io/gnzsnz/ib-gateway:stable   # or :latest; tws-rdesktop likewise: docker pull ghcr.io/gnzsnz/tws-rdesktop:stable

install.method: Build from source with Compose (README tells you to edit the Dockerfile first; those steps are stale, see claim_checks)
Contributor local build of the sample compose file

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - Dockerfile.template:28-34 selects the x64 installer unless `uname -m` is aarch64; ubuntu:24.04 base (Dockerfile.template:9,63); CI and publish build linux/amd64 (.github/workflows/build.yml:54; .github/workflows/publish.yml:70,99).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - README, CONTRIBUTING and the workflows never mention WSL or Windows (grep; the only hit is a generic 'OS: [e.g. Windows]' prompt at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md:66). It is a Linux container, so behaviour depends on the user's Docker engine, which upstream does not document.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes (container only, as claimed by the README) - README.md:31 and 580-600 state aarch64 support for M1/M2/M3 and that `docker compose up` pulls the matching image; Dockerfile.template:28-33 picks the arm installer; publish.yml:70,99 publishes linux/arm64. No native macOS build or macOS-specific instruction exists. CI builds arm64 under QEMU (build.yml:27-30,54) but never runs it; README.md:583-585 warns the TWS image 'might have unexpected bugs'.
platforms.gpu: no - not applicable: IB Gateway runs headless on Xvfb (README.md:17-18) with software rendering; only the TWS compose maps /dev/dri for desktop rendering (tws-docker-compose.yml:5-6; README.md:259); no CUDA or compute use found.

integrations.cli: No project CLI. Operated through `docker compose up` (README.md:165-167) and `docker exec ... pkill -x socat|ssh` for troubleshooting (README.md:560-578). Maintainer-only script `update.sh <channel> <version>` regenerates stable/ and latest/ (update.sh:6-32). IBC's command server is disabled by default (CommandServerPort=0, image-files/config/ibc/config.ini.tmpl:826).
integrations.mcp: none found (grep for mcp, claude, codex, agents.md, anthropic, openai, llm across the tree outside .git returned no matches).
integrations.sdk_or_api: No SDK or HTTP API. The service exposes IBKR's TWS API as a raw, unencrypted TCP socket: gateway live 4001 / paper 4002 inside the container, republished by socat on 4003/4004 (README.md:231-236; image-files/scripts/common.sh:93-103); TWS 7496/7497 republished on 7498/7499 (README.md:239-243; common.sh:109-119); VNC 5900 (README.md:235); RDP 3389 for TWS (README.md:243). Clients are third-party, e.g. ib_insync (README.md:438).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found (same grep as mcp; no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or .claude/ files in the tree).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home code found: the runtime scripts contain no curl/wget or outbound calls beyond starting Xvfb, x11vnc, socat, ssh and IBC (image-files/scripts/run.sh:48-91; common.sh:143-265; tws-scripts/*.sh). Required accounts/network at runtime: an Interactive Brokers account (TWS_USERID / TWS_PASSWORD, docker-compose.yml:11-12; README.md:181-182) and outbound connectivity from the proprietary IB Gateway/IBC to IBKR servers (not inspectable in this repo); the shipped jts.ini template sets UseSSL=true and s3store=true (image-files/config/ibgateway/jts.ini.tmpl:10-11), and the IBC template says 'Store settings on server' keeps a copy of TWS settings on IB's servers and does not apply to Gateway (config.ini.tmpl:270-285, value left empty). Inbound listeners in the container: socat on 4003/4004 (7498/7499 for TWS) on all interfaces (image-files/scripts/run_socat.sh:12), x11vnc on 5900 only when a VNC password is set (run.sh:57-69), xrdp 3389 in the TWS image (README.md:243). Optional outbound: ssh client to the user-supplied SSH_USER_TUNNEL host when SSH_TUNNEL is yes/both (common.sh:151-160,214-248; run_ssh.sh:13). Build-time network: Ubuntu apt mirrors (Dockerfile.template:23-27,86-95), this repo's GitHub release assets (Dockerfile.template:15,34-39), the IBC release at github.com/IbcAlpha/IBC (Dockerfile.template:17-18,47), and ghcr.io/gnzsnz/ib-gateway plus lscr.io/linuxserver/rdesktop base images (Dockerfile.tws.template:11,19). Maintainer CI: daily polling of download2.interactivebrokers.com (detect-releases.yml:26,51) and IBC releases (detect-ibc-release.yml:37); publishing to ghcr.io and Docker Hub with DOCKERHUB_USERNAME/DOCKERHUB_TOKEN secrets (publish.yml:36-47).

entry_points.what: Compose project 'algo-trader' with one service, ib-gateway (build ./latest, image ghcr.io/gnzsnz/ib-gateway:latest, restart: always, ports bound to 127.0.0.1); run with `docker compose up`.
Compose file with one service, tws (build ./latest, Dockerfile.tws; /dev/dri, shm_size 1gb, seccomp:unconfined, bind ./config:/config, named volume tws_tmp, ports 127.0.0.1:7496/7497/3370).
Two-stage ubuntu:24.04 build of the ib-gateway image; rendered by update.sh into stable/Dockerfile and latest/Dockerfile (the actual build contexts); CMD is <private> (line 109).
Container entrypoint for ib-gateway: start scripts, Xvfb, ssh-agent, optional x11vnc, config rendering, socat/ssh forwarding, IBC launch (`ibcstart.sh -g`), live+paper dual mode, SIGTERM trap.
Shared functions: apply_settings (envsubst of config templates), file_env/unset_env (_FILE secrets), set_ports, set_java_heap, port_forwarding, setup_ssh/start_ssh, start_socat, run_scripts.
s6 custom service for the TWS image (installed as /custom-services.d/start_session.sh): sets the abc user password, opens an xrdp session, then execs tws-scripts/run_tws.sh as abc.
Maintainer script `./update.sh <stable|latest> <version>`: copies image-files/ into the channel directory and renders Dockerfile.template / Dockerfile.tws.template with envsubst (update.sh:20-32).
Release pipeline: on pushed tags v*, builds and pushes ib-gateway and tws-rdesktop multi-arch images to ghcr.io and Docker Hub.

code.architecture: Packaging repo, no application code. image-files/ is the source of truth (CONTRIBUTING.md:29-35): scripts/ (run.sh, common.sh, run_socat.sh, run_ssh.sh), tws-scripts/ (start_session.sh, run_tws.sh) and config templates (config/ibc/config.ini.tmpl, 960 lines; config/ibgateway/jts.ini.tmpl). update.sh copies image-files/ into stable/ or latest/ and renders the Dockerfile templates; the committed per-channel directories are the Docker build contexts (docker-compose.yml:6; publish.yml:71). Non-empty line counts of every script/config file are identical in image-files/, latest/ and stable/ (grep count). ib-gateway image: setup stage downloads the IB Gateway installer from this repo's release assets (sha256-checked) and the IBC 3.24.2 zip and installs them under /root/Jts and /root/ibc; final stage adds socat, xvfb, x11vnc, ssh client and GTK/X libraries, creates non-root user ibgateway (uid/gid 1000) with passwordless sudo, CMD run.sh (Dockerfile.template:9-109). run.sh order: START_SCRIPTS, Xvfb :1, setup_ssh, Java heap, x11vnc, X_SCRIPTS, then start_process = set_ports -> apply_settings (envsubst config.ini.tmpl/jts.ini.tmpl, common.sh:4-39) -> port_forwarding (socat 4003/4004 -> 127.0.0.1:4001/4002, or `ssh -R` tunnel) -> IBC ibcstart.sh -g launching IB Gateway -> IBC_SCRIPTS -> wait with SIGTERM trap (run.sh:93-194); TRADING_MODE=both runs live then paper after sleep 15 (run.sh:135-185). tws-rdesktop image: FROM lscr.io/linuxserver/rdesktop:ubuntu-xfce, copies Jts and ibc from the ib-gateway image, runs run_tws.sh under xrdp as user abc (Dockerfile.tws.template:11,19,54-59). Neither Dockerfile defines HEALTHCHECK, EXPOSE, VOLUME or ENTRYPOINT (grep), and no 'health' string exists anywhere in the repo.
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts are container images only: ghcr.io/gnzsnz/ib-gateway, gnzsnz/ib-gateway (Docker Hub), ghcr.io/gnzsnz/tws-rdesktop, gnzsnz/tws-rdesktop (publish.yml:57-59, 86-88), linux/amd64 + linux/arm64 (publish.yml:70,99). Release trigger is a pushed git tag matching v* (publish.yml:3-6); the channel is the second dash-separated field of the tag name (publish.yml:22); docker/metadata-action type=match patterns yield mutable tags <major.minor> and <channel> plus the full version (publish.yml:62-65, flavor latest=false). IB installers are released separately: detect-releases.yml runs daily at 06:00 UTC (L3-5), reads IB's version.json (L26), downloads x64 and arm installers from download2.interactivebrokers.com, writes a .sha256 with sha256sum (L48-55), creates GitHub release ibgateway-<channel>@<version> with those assets (L62-65), runs update.sh and opens a PR (L67-118). Integrity: sha256 of the installer is checked at image build (Dockerfile.template:39-40) but the checksum comes from the same release; the IBC zip has no checksum (Dockerfile.template:47-49). Signatures/attestations: none configured; grep of .github for cosign, attest, sbom, provenance, sigstore, gpg found no matches.
code.tests_and_ci: No test framework and no test files (approx. 0; glob for test*/tests/*_test.*/*.bats and a grep of the workflows found none). Five workflows in .github/workflows: on-push-n-pr.yml (push to any branch except update-*-to-* and IBC-update*, PRs to master, manual; matrix stable/latest calling build.yml); build.yml (reusable: QEMU+Buildx, builds ib-gateway for linux/amd64+arm64 without pushing, builds TWS for amd64 only using a local ib-gateway image handoff, GHA cache; never starts a container); publish.yml (on v* tags: multi-arch build+push to GHCR and Docker Hub); detect-releases.yml and detect-ibc-release.yml (daily cron jobs that open PRs for new IB Gateway / IBC versions). Lint tooling exists only as .pre-commit-config.yaml (trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, check-yaml, check-added-large-files, shebang/executable checks, shellcheck, shfmt, hadolint, markdownlint, dotenv-linter) and is not invoked by any workflow (grep). .github/dependabot.yml tracks docker in /stable and /latest daily and github-actions weekly.
code.dependencies: No language package manifests (glob found no package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml, Gemfile, pom.xml, lock files). Declared dependencies: Dockerfile.template - 1 base image (ubuntu:24.04, two stages), 2 version-pinned downloads (IB Gateway installer per channel, IBC 3.24.2 zip), apt packages 3 (setup stage) + 36 (runtime stage), unpinned (hadolint DL3008 ignored, line 8); Dockerfile.tws.template - 2 base images (ghcr.io/gnzsnz/ib-gateway:${IB_VERSION}, lscr.io/linuxserver/rdesktop:ubuntu-xfce) + 40 apt packages; .github/workflows/*.yml - 6 third-party actions pinned by major tag (actions/checkout@v7, docker/setup-buildx-action@v4, docker/setup-qemu-action@v4, docker/metadata-action@v6, docker/build-push-action@v7, docker/login-action@v4) plus 1 local reusable workflow; .pre-commit-config.yaml - 5 hook repositories. Not in the repo: Docker Engine with Compose, the proprietary IB Gateway/TWS binaries, an IBKR account.
code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md anywhere (glob for SECURITY*/security* found nothing; .github/ holds only ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, dependabot.yml and workflows/). README.md:367-509 has user-facing 'Security Considerations' guidance, which is not a vulnerability-reporting policy.

claim_checks.claim: Compose is how the service is defined and run: create docker-compose.yml and .env, then `docker compose up` (README.md:163-167, 597).
claim_checks.evidence: docker-compose.yml:1-57 and tws-docker-compose.yml:1-69 are Compose-format files (top-level `name: algo-trader`, `services:`), run with `docker compose up` / `docker compose -f tws-docker-compose.yml up` (README.md:166,597). Upstream support also requires `docker compose config` and `docker compose logs` output (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md:29-34,51,60). No Swarm, Kubernetes, Helm or Podman references in README, CONTRIBUTING, .github or the compose files (grep). Scope of what the files define: docker-compose.yml has one service (ib-gateway), no networks/secrets/healthcheck/depends_on/env_file keys, and its volumes are commented out (L48-53); tws-docker-compose.yml has one service (tws), bind mount ./config:/config and named volume tws_tmp (L56-58, 68-69). Variables come from .env through ${VAR} interpolation (docker-compose.yml:11-47). Docs mix `docker compose` (README.md:166,594,597) and legacy `docker-compose` (README.md:663; CONTRIBUTING.md:65,75).

claim_checks.claim: Sample compose exposes API/VNC ports only on 127.0.0.1 of the docker host (README.md:245-247, 376-377).
claim_checks.evidence: docker-compose.yml:54-57 binds 127.0.0.1:4001->4003, 127.0.0.1:4002->4004, 127.0.0.1:5900; tws-docker-compose.yml:63-66 binds 127.0.0.1:7496, 7497 and 3370. Caveat in code: socat inside the container listens on all interfaces (image-files/scripts/run_socat.sh:12) while jts.ini only trusts 127.0.0.1 (image-files/config/ibgateway/jts.ini.tmpl:3), so any container on the same Docker network can reach the 4003/4004 (7498/7499) trading ports; README.md:399-401 acknowledges this for its `trader` network example.

claim_checks.claim: Runs IB Gateway and TWS 'without any human interaction' (README.md:9-10).
claim_checks.evidence: IBC logs in and answers dialogs from env-rendered config (image-files/scripts/run.sh:82-86; image-files/config/ibc/config.ini.tmpl:83-88). But the IBC template says IBKR Mobile second-factor approval is still required and can time out (config.ini.tmpl:118-122), that auto-restart avoids 2FA only after the initial login (config.ini.tmpl:564-575), and that the weekly Sunday cold restart should be timed so the user can handle 2FA alerts on live accounts (config.ini.tmpl:624-631). Compose defaults TWOFA_TIMEOUT_ACTION to exit (docker-compose.yml:21) together with `restart: always` (docker-compose.yml:4); README.md:191,195 documents these options. There is no HEALTHCHECK anywhere in the repo (grep for 'health' found nothing).

claim_checks.claim: No credentials are stored in the image; they come from env vars, with Docker secrets via _FILE (README.md:513-520).
claim_checks.evidence: Nothing is baked into the image (Dockerfile.template has no credential), but at start apply_settings renders IbLoginId/IbPassword into ${IBC_INI} inside the container with chmod 600 (image-files/scripts/common.sh:9-14; config.ini.tmpl:83-88), and unset_env only unsets a variable when its _FILE variant was used (common.sh:63-71), so a password passed as TWS_PASSWORD stays in the container environment. _FILE support is real: file_env (common.sh:45-61) is applied to TWS_PASSWORD (common.sh:9), VNC_SERVER_PASSWORD (run.sh:61), SSH_PASSPHRASE (common.sh:181), PASSWD (image-files/tws-scripts/start_session.sh:13) and TWS_PASSWORD_PAPER (image-files/tws-scripts/run_tws.sh:141; ib-gateway path run.sh:166-171); there is no _FILE variant for TWS_USERID. Neither sample compose file passes any *_FILE variable (docker-compose.yml:10-47; tws-docker-compose.yml:16-55); the README's embedded example adds only TWS_PASSWORD_FILE (README.md:70) and its secrets example sets the others directly (README.md:529-547).

claim_checks.claim: Parallel live and paper trading in one container (README.md:29, 184-187).
claim_checks.evidence: image-files/scripts/run.sh:135-185: TRADING_MODE=both starts live first with `_live`-suffixed IBC ini and settings path, then paper (TWS_USERID_PAPER plus TWS_PASSWORD_PAPER or its _FILE) after `sleep 15`; image-files/tws-scripts/run_tws.sh:116-171 does the same for TWS. Ports follow the mode: gateway live 4001/4003, paper 4002/4004; TWS live 7496/7498, paper 7497/7499 (common.sh:89-129). docker-compose.yml:14-15 passes the paper credentials but not TWS_PASSWORD_PAPER_FILE; the README's embedded compose example omits TWS_USERID_PAPER, TWS_PASSWORD_PAPER and the *_FILE variables (README.md:67-103), so `both` needs them added to environment:.

claim_checks.claim: Settings persist via TWS_SETTINGS_PATH plus a volume; TIME_ZONE is applied only when jts.ini does not exist (README.md:202-203, 303-327).
claim_checks.evidence: image-files/scripts/common.sh:16-35 creates $TWS_SETTINGS_PATH with plain `mkdir` (no -p) if missing and renders jts.ini from the template only if the file is absent. By default state stays in the container's writable layer: docker-compose.yml:48-53 has every volume commented out, whereas tws-docker-compose.yml:57-58 mounts ./config:/config and tws_tmp:/tmp. .gitignore:1-8 ignores /.env, tws_settings/, ssh/, /config/, /*_password.txt and /init-scripts/*.

claim_checks.claim: The Dockerfile pulls the installer from this project's releases so a specific version can be rebuilt; build-from-source steps in README.md:604-663.
claim_checks.evidence: Installer part matches code: Dockerfile.template:33-40 downloads ibgateway-<ver>-standalone-linux-<x64|arm>.sh and its .sha256 from releases/download/ibgateway-<channel>%40<ver>/ and runs sha256sum --check; the assets are created by .github/workflows/detect-releases.yml:48-65. Reproducibility is only partial: ubuntu:24.04 is not digest-pinned and `apt-get upgrade -y` runs at build (Dockerfile.template:9,63,87), the IBC 3.24.2 zip is fetched without a checksum (Dockerfile.template:47-49), and the .sha256 is generated by the workflow that uploads the installer (detect-releases.yml:54). The README's build steps are stale versus code (code wins): they point to a root `Dockerfile` (README.md:605,621) and a gh-pages raw URL for x64 only (README.md:622-625,642-646), but the tree has no root Dockerfile (generated Dockerfiles live in stable/ and latest/, rendered from Dockerfile.template by update.sh:20-32) and the real URL is the release-asset URL with arch selection (Dockerfile.template:28-39).

Matches the tree: latest/Dockerfile:11 = 10.51.1a, stable/Dockerfile:11 = 10.50.1e, Dockerfile.template:13 = IBC 3.24.2; image tags derive from git tags v<version>-<channel> via metadata-action (publish.yml:62-65). But the revision under review is tag ibgateway-latest@10.51.1b (.git/packed-refs:2), whose tree still pins 10.51.1a. That tag form is created by detect-releases.yml:62, which runs before update.sh (L69) and the PR step (L118) (inference: the tag marks the installer-asset release made before the version-bump PR), and it does not match publish.yml's v* trigger (publish.yml:3-6), so no image build is tied to this tag.

claim_checks.claim: TWS (from 10.26.1h) is provided as the tws-rdesktop image (README.md:15, 249-251).
claim_checks.evidence: Dockerfile.tws.template builds on lscr.io/linuxserver/rdesktop:ubuntu-xfce (L19) and starts an xrdp session then run_tws.sh as user abc (image-files/tws-scripts/start_session.sh:32,45), but it copies <private> and <private> out of the ib-gateway image (Dockerfile.tws.template:11,55-56). No workflow or Dockerfile downloads a TWS installer: only ibgateway-*-standalone-linux-* installers are fetched (detect-releases.yml:48-55); TWS URLs appear only as README links and the version.json lookup (detect-releases.yml:26). JAVA_HEAP_SIZE edits ibgateway.vmoptions under ${TWS_PATH}/ibgateway/<ver> (common.sh:134-136) and run_tws.sh calls ibcstart.sh without -g (run_tws.sh:49-53, versus run.sh:82). Whether the copied tree runs TWS cannot be determined from this repo (IBKR binaries and IBC are not in it); README.md:582-585 itself says the official arm installer is for ib-gateway and the TWS image 'might have unexpected bugs'.

claim_checks.claim: SSH tunnel variables SSH_ALIVE_COUNT, SSH_REMOTE_PORT and SSH_VNC_PORT behave as in the configuration table (README.md:211,214,217).
claim_checks.evidence: Code wins where they differ. SSH_ALIVE_COUNT: README says default not defined, code defaults to 3 (image-files/scripts/common.sh:172). SSH_REMOTE_PORT / SSH_VNC_PORT: README describes them as the remote port, but run_ssh.sh:13 builds `ssh -R 127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}:localhost:${SSH_REMOTE_PORT}` and common.sh:234 builds `-R 127.0.0.1:5900:localhost:$SSH_VNC_PORT`; by ssh -R argument order the first port is the remote listening port and host:port is the local target, so only values equal to the API port / 5900 forward to a listening local port (inference from ssh syntax, not executed). Confirmed as documented: ssh client only, no sshd (Dockerfile.template:89; run_ssh.sh:13), automatic tunnel restart after SSH_RESTART seconds, default 5 (run_ssh.sh:14), ServerAliveInterval default 20 (common.sh:171).

risks: Proprietary payload with self-asserted integrity: the images wrap IBKR's closed-source IB Gateway installer, re-hosted as release assets of this repo (detect-releases.yml:48-65) and executed as root at build (Dockerfile.template:38-42). The only integrity check is a .sha256 generated by the same workflow and stored in the same release (detect-releases.yml:54; Dockerfile.template:39-40); the IBC zip is unzipped with no checksum (Dockerfile.template:47-49). No file in the repo states IBKR's licence terms for redistributing the installers (grep of README, CONTRIBUTING, Dockerfile templates, .github).

Licence metadata conflict: LICENSE and the README badge say MIT (LICENSE:1; README.md:3), but both image Dockerfiles label org.opencontainers.image.licenses as 'Apache License Version 2.0' (Dockerfile.template:114; Dockerfile.tws.template:69; latest/Dockerfile:114; stable/Dockerfile:114; latest/Dockerfile.tws:69).

Unattended operation is conditional: IBKR 2FA and the weekly cold restart can need a human (config.ini.tmpl:118-122, 564-575, 624-631). Compose default TWOFA_TIMEOUT_ACTION=exit with restart: always (docker-compose.yml:4,21) means an unanswered prompt ends the process and Docker restarts it, i.e. a new login attempt (inference). No HEALTHCHECK exists in the Dockerfiles or Compose files (grep), so Compose cannot tell 'container running' from 'logged in'.

Credential surface: the password is rendered in plain text into IBC config.ini inside the container (chmod 600) (common.sh:9-14) and stays in the environment unless a _FILE variable was used (common.sh:63-71); the VNC password is passed on the x11vnc command line (run.sh:64-65); the runtime user has passwordless sudo (Dockerfile.template:101); the TWS desktop user abc gets password 'abc' unless PASSWD is set (image-files/tws-scripts/start_session.sh:13-16; README.md:221); .env-dist ships placeholder passwords (.env-dist:8-9,66); there is no _FILE option for TWS_USERID.

Deployment scope is controlled only by Compose port/network settings: the IB API is unencrypted and unauthenticated (README.md:371-374), socat listens on all container interfaces (image-files/scripts/run_socat.sh:12) so any container on the same network reaches live/paper trading ports, and removing the 127.0.0.1 prefix exposes them to the host network (README.md:247, 389-397; docker-compose.yml:54-57). The TWS compose also sets seccomp:unconfined and maps /dev/dri (tws-docker-compose.yml:5-9).

Reproducibility and supply chain: floating inputs (ubuntu:24.04 tag, apt-get upgrade -y at build, unpinned apt packages with DL3008 ignored, lscr.io/linuxserver/rdesktop:ubuntu-xfce) (Dockerfile.template:8-9,63,87; Dockerfile.tws.template:8,19); the sample compose uses the mutable image tag ghcr.io/gnzsnz/ib-gateway:latest (docker-compose.yml:9) and published tags <channel> and <major.minor> are mutable (publish.yml:62-65); GitHub Actions are pinned by major tag, not commit SHA (build.yml:22-50); no signing, SBOM or provenance step in the workflows (grep of .github).

Assurance and docs drift: roughly 0 test files; CI only builds images and never starts a container (build.yml; no docker run / compose up in any workflow) and does not run the pre-commit linters, although the bug template says the sample compose files 'are tested' (bug_report.md:29-31). README build-from-source steps and SSH variable defaults differ from the code (see claim_checks 7 and 10); the revision tag ibgateway-latest@10.51.1b points at a tree pinning 10.51.1a (.git/packed-refs:2; latest/Dockerfile:11). Upstream support is limited to the container itself, not IBKR or IBC problems (bug_report.md:80-82).

Platform and scope limits: Linux containers only, no WSL2/Windows/native macOS instructions (README.md:31, 580-600 mention only aarch64 images); arm64 images are built under QEMU and never executed in CI (build.yml:27-30,54; publish.yml:28-31), and the README warns the TWS arm image 'might have unexpected bugs' (README.md:583-585). How TWS binaries get into tws-rdesktop is not visible in the tree (Dockerfile.tws.template:11,55-56; claim_checks 9). Each Compose file defines a single service; supporting services such as Jupyter Quant or an SSH bastion are only mentioned in prose (README.md:428-441).
